newsitem.title: CHINA: Top China official says HK handover going smoothly.
newsitem.headline: Top China official says HK handover going smoothly.

text.p: Vice Premier Qian Qichen, China's top official handling this year's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong, said on Thursday the transfer of power was going well.

"During the transitional period, I don't know how many so-called crises of confidence have occurred," said Qian, who is foreign minister and heads Beijing's Preparatory Committee handling the handover.
"But as I can see, the situation is now quite good," Qian told reporters before beginning a meeting of the standing members of the Preparatory Committee in Beijing.
"I am confident in Hong Kong," he said.
Quoting from Chinese author Lu Xun, Qian said the committee was working as hard as an ox to achieve a smooth handover of the British colony, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
The Preparatory Committee is the China-appointed caucus responsible for shaping Hong Kong's future when China resumes sovereignty after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
High on the agenda of the two-day meeting will be a proposal to repeal several of Hong Kong's laws on civil liberties, including part of the Bill of Rights.
The plan sparked outrage in Hong Kong. Britain has lodged a strong protest against the proposal.
